steps.title: High and cool
steps.body: The Valle de Uco lies about 100 km south-west of Mendoza city, at 900 to over 1,600 m, right against the Andes. Its three departments are Tupungato, Tunuyán and San Carlos. Since the 1990s, it's become Argentina's most acclaimed area for fine wine, with major investment, including from French and American producers.

steps.title: Altitude
steps.body: Altitude cools the air by about 0.6 degrees per 100 m and strengthens ultraviolet light. Cool nights preserve acidity and aroma; strong UV thickens skins, adding colour and tannin. Valle de Uco Malbec is fresher, more floral and more structured than in Luján. Soils, alluvial with stones and limestone, vary greatly.

steps.prompt: How does Valle de Uco Malbec usually compare with Luján de Cuyo's?

steps.title: Geographical indications
steps.body: Since 2013, the Valle de Uco has recognised smaller GIs: Paraje Altamira, in San Carlos, with limestone-rich alluvial soils; Gualtallary, in Tupungato, high up to 1,600 m with limestone; Los Chacayes, in Tunuyán; and San Pablo, very high and cool. These help show terroir in Argentine wine.

steps.prompt: Match each GI to its department.
steps.explanation: The Valle de Uco has a growing map of GIs.

steps.title: What you learned
points: The Valle de Uco is high, against the Andes
Altitude gives fresher, more structured Malbec
GIs like Gualtallary and Paraje Altamira show terroir
